In this work, Zircaloy-4 alloy was successfully fabricated via LPBF technology. The microstructure evolution and deformation behavior of the alloy were systematically investigated under uniaxial tensile loading at both room temperature (RT) and an elevated temperature of 380 ◦C.
Commercial sheet Zircaloy-4 alloy, produced via conventional rolling followed by annealing, was also examined as a counterpart.

evidence.quote: A BLT-S210 LPBF machine (Xi’an Bright Laser Technologies Co., China) was used to fabricate Zircaloy-4 samples. Two geometries with dimensions of 45 mm (length, L) × 8 mm (width, W) × 6 mm (height, H) were fabricated along the Z-direction (building direction, BD), as illustrated in Fig. 1c. An argon-filled chamber was used to maintain oxygen levels below 150 ppm during processing to prevent oxidation. Optimized parameters for LPBF of Zircaloy-4 was listed in Table 2.

The precipitates or SPPs enhance the strength of alloy by obstructing dislocation motion. Therefore, it is reasonable to conclude that nanoscale enriched Fe and Cr SPPs hinder dislocation motion and reduce plastic deformation under tensile loading, which macroscopically results in a higher strength (σy and σUTS) of LPBF-processed Zircaloy-4 alloy.
The GND density increased, promoting dislocation entanglement (Fig. 7i), which hindered deformation and enhanced the strength of the Zircaloy-4 alloy, after tensile testing at RT and 380 ◦C HT.
The fine α lath with submicron widths serve as the foundational microstructural units responsible for the high strength of Zircaloy-4 alloy under RT and 380 ◦C HT tensile loading.
